parsed.summary: The file states four results. (1) The centered simplex (n+1)Δn − (1,…,1) has barycenter 0. (2) For n > 0 its volume is (n+1)^n/n!. (3) For n > 0 there is a compact convex full-dimensional body with barycenter 0 whose only interior lattice point is 0 and whose volume equals (n+1)^n/n!. (4) Every such body has volume strictly less than (n+1)^n/n!. The most important caveat: the main theorem uses a strict inequality `<`, while the paper proves `≤` and says the bound is sharp. Theorem (4) is false, and it directly contradicts theorem (3) as stated in the same file.

glossary.plain: ℝ^n modelled as Fin n → ℝ, with sup-norm topology and product Lebesgue measure
glossary.note: Same topology and Lebesgue measure as Euclidean ℝ^n.

glossary.plain: Lebesgue volume of K, as a real number (∞ is sent to 0)
glossary.note: Finite for compact K, so the ∞ ↦ 0 convention never applies here.
For compact K with nonempty interior, the volume is positive and the integral converges.

glossary.plain: the set of z ∈ ℤ^n with z ∈ int K
a convex compact set with nonempty interior, barycenter 0, and int K ∩ ℤ^n = {0}

lean_claims.plain: For all n, the barycenter of (n+1)Δn − 1 is 0.
For n > 0, there exists a convex compact full-dimensional K with barycenter 0, int K ∩ ℤ^n = {0}, and vol K = (n+1)^n/n!.
For n > 0, every convex compact S with nonempty interior, barycenter 0, and int S ∩ ℤ^n = {0} satisfies vol S < (n+1)^n/n! (strict inequality).

paper_claims.plain: If K is a full-dimensional compact convex body with barycenter 0 and int K ∩ ℤ^n = {0}, then vol K ≤ (n+1)^n/n!.
The simplex (n+1)Δn − (1,…,1) has barycenter 0, has no other interior lattice point, and has volume (n+1)^n/n!.

coverage.why: Lean asserts strict `<`. This is stronger than the paper's `≤` and is false, because the equality case exists.
Gives an extremal body; together with the two simplex lemmas it matches the sharpness remark.

flags.explanation: The conclusion uses `<` instead of `≤`. The paper explicitly states the bound is attained by the centered simplex. The body supplied by exists_centeredBody_sharp (line 56) satisfies every hypothesis of this theorem yet has volume exactly sharpConstant n. So the strict statement is false and contradicts another target theorem. If both were actually kernel-checked, the environment would be inconsistent, or some proof would rely on sorry or an extra axiom. The statement should read `≤`.
flags.probe_idea: example (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : False := by obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := Ehrhart.SimplexVolume.exists_centeredBody_sharp n hn; have := Ehrhart.Volume.ehrhart_volume_inequality_for_sets hn K.carrier K.convex K.compact K.fullDimensional K.centered K.uniqueInteriorLatticePoint; unfold Ehrhart.sharpConstant at hK; linarith
